reported_claims.text: The ruling junta postponed the presidential and legislative elections due on 6 December by two years, to 26 November 2028.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Decree signed by transitional president General Horta N'Tam

reported_claims.text: The decree cites insufficient technical, material and financial conditions for the vote; a new electoral census and mapping are required, constituencies fall from 29 to 12 and parliament shrinks from 102 to 65 members.
N'Tam said in a televised address that the process must guarantee legality, transparency, inclusivity and credibility, and that first-ever municipal elections would be held.

title: Guinea-Bissau junta postpones elections by two years to 2028
summary: Guinea-Bissau's military rulers postponed presidential and legislative elections that were due on 6 December by two years, to 26 November 2028, citing insufficient technical, material and financial conditions. The announcement came on the first anniversary of the 26 November 2025 coup that overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embalo and extends military-led rule to three years.
impact_assessment: Potential: prolonged military rule, friction with ECOWAS, and a further entrenchment of junta-led transitions in West Africa.
priority_rationale: MODERATE: a significant setback to a return to civilian rule; no violence or unrest reported.
monitoring_actions: Watch for opposition mobilisation in Bissau
